assessment.nobel_worthiness: A theoretical prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle followed by a clean experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states. It opened an entire field of moire quantum matter. This is the pattern I value most: theory led to a clue found in nature, and nature answered.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the decisive 2011 continuum-model prediction and Jarillo-Herrero's group made the 2018 experimental discovery. Cao and collaborators are not credited in the supplied names, which may complicate the experimental side; as I recall, a prize could still be framed around prediction plus discovery.
assessment.maturity: Many independent groups have reproduced the phenomena and the field is large and stable. Recognition seems timely, though the nature of the superconductivity is still debated.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism of twisted-graphene superconductivity is unresolved.
Early-experiment credit may extend beyond the supplied names.
Sample-dependence and reproducibility details are recalled from memory, not verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators changed how condensed matter physics classifies phases. The quantum spin Hall effect was predicted and then observed in HgTe quantum wells, a clean case of an idea confirmed by experiment with wide reach into materials and quantum devices.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical proposals. Molenkamp's group did the first experimental observation, which follows the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. The omission of Zhang and of the 3D-materials experimentalists is a real allocation problem; a three-person prize is plausible but not obviously fair.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently over about fifteen years in several material families, and the interpretation is stable. It is mature and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Credit for the HgTe proposal and 3D topological insulators (Fu, Kane, Mele, Moore, Balents, Hasan, Zhang) is split.
Whether the committee would treat the theory and the HgTe experiment as one discovery or two.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The detection of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos opened a new window on the cosmos and gave evidence on cosmic-ray sources, including the 2018 TXS 0506+056 association and the Galactic plane. This is a genuine discovery from nature with an existential flavour, in line with the observational discoveries I want to reward.
assessment.attribution: Halzen led the IceCube concept and the collaboration science. Karle and Spiering are central, but the collaboration is large and the AMANDA lineage and earlier proposals (Markov, Reines, DUMAND) complicate credit. A configuration from the supplied names is defensible but imperfect.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is firmly confirmed, and ANTARES/KM3NeT and later IceCube analyses support the picture. Source identification is still partial, so the physics is mature in detection and young in astrophysical interpretation.
uncertainties: Source identification beyond TXS 0506+056 and NGC 1068 is incomplete.
Credit within a very large collaboration and across predecessor experiments.
Whether the 2002 prize for neutrino astronomy is seen as covering the ground.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The first horizon-scale images of the M87 and Sgr A* shadows are direct clues from nature about strong-field gravity, building on the 2020 black hole prize. For someone working on black holes and quantum gravity, the images are striking, although they confirm expectations more than they overturn them.
assessment.attribution: Doeleman led the EHT, Falcke proposed the shadow imaging concept, and Moran led earlier VLBI mm development. The 200-plus-member collaboration and the key imaging and calibration contributions make the personal attribution genuinely contentious.
assessment.maturity: Repeated observation of M87 across epochs and the Sgr A* image support the results. Polarisation and tests of GR alternatives are still evolving, so recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Diffuse attribution within a large collaboration.
Image reconstruction choices and prior dependence.
Limited constraints on horizonless alternatives so far.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental discovery of the Higgs boson completed the Standard Model, a landmark clue from nature that confirmed a decades-old theoretical idea. The theory was already honoured in 2013, but the experimental discovery and detector achievement have lasting importance.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread over thousands of people. Gianotti, Jenni and Virdee were the spokespeople or founders of ATLAS and CMS around the discovery, and Evans led the LHC construction. Choosing three from five credited names is arbitrary on scientific grounds, and the prize rules complicate recognising an accelerator or a collaboration.
assessment.maturity: Properties of the Higgs have been measured to a few percent in several channels and the interpretation is stable. It is mature, but the committee may see the 2013 prize as having closed the matter.
uncertainties: Whether a second Higgs prize is acceptable to the committee.
Allocation among the ATLAS, CMS and accelerator contributors.
Individual versus collaboration credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and realised with Ye's spectroscopy, reach 10^-18 fractional uncertainty. They are a transformative precision tool for tests of fundamental physics, geodesy and the future redefinition of the second.
assessment.attribution: Katori made the decisive magic-wavelength idea and first lattice clock, and Ye achieved the leading performance. Ye also overlaps with the frequency-comb lineage already recognised in 2005. A two-person prize looks clean from the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Many laboratories have reproduced the clocks and metrological use is under way. The field is mature, though the redefinition of the second has not yet happened.
uncertainties: Overlap with ion clocks (Wineland's 2012 prize) and frequency combs (2005).
Whether the committee prefers to wait for the redefinition of the second.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Precision CMB mapping with WMAP and Planck fixed the parameters of the Lambda-CDM model, giving the observational foundation for dark energy and dark matter. I know the importance well, since the dark energy question is central to my own work, but the 2006 and 2019 prizes already covered related ground.
assessment.attribution: WMAP's leadership (Bennett, Page, Spergel) is a natural trio. The Planck team (Puget and others) and earlier ground and balloon experiments complicate the story, and collaboration work dominates.
assessment.maturity: Results are confirmed by independent satellites and ground experiments and are very stable, although tensions such as the Hubble tension linger.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2006 COBE prize and the 2011 and 2019 cosmology prizes.
Planck versus WMAP credit.
Hubble tension and other anomalies might reopen interpretation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation with ultracold atoms in optical lattices, including the Mott-superfluid transition and the Hubbard model realised in the laboratory, made strongly correlated quantum matter experimentally controllable. It is a clear case of theory proposals paired with demonstration.
assessment.attribution: Zoller and Jaksch proposed the Hubbard-model realisation, and Greiner with Bloch and Hansch achieved the Mott transition. Esslinger's fermionic work is also decisive, and Jaksch is absent from the names. A three-person selection leaves out someone important.
assessment.maturity: The field is widely replicated and has developed into quantum gas microscopes and digital-analogue simulators. It is mature, though the 2001 and 2012 prizes covered nearby ground.
uncertainties: Overlap with BEC and single-quantum-system prizes.
Allocation among Bloch, Greiner, Esslinger and Zoller, and the omission of Jaksch.
Whether the committee would rather prize a later quantum-computing application.
